title: A Bowl with a Friend
source_body:
Last Saturday, I went to a malatang restaurant with my friend Mina. It was my first time there, so I did not know what to choose.

"First, pick the things you want to eat," Mina said.

I put noodles, cabbage, mushrooms, and tofu into my bowl. Everything looked delicious. Then I reached for more noodles.

"Your bowl is already full!" Mina said with a laugh.

We both chose the mild soup. However, when I took my first bite, it was still a little spicy for me. I drank some water and ate more slowly.

"Next time, I'll choose less spicy soup," I said.

Mina smiled. "And fewer noodles?"

I looked at my big bowl and laughed. The food was good, but eating with Mina was the best part.

Last Saturday, I went to a malatang restaurant with my friend Mina. It was my first time there, so I needed help choosing my food. "Pick the things you want to eat," Mina explained.

I put noodles, cabbage, mushrooms, and tofu into my bowl. Everything looked so delicious that I reached for more noodles. "Your bowl is already full!" Mina said with a laugh. I looked down and noticed how much food I had chosen.

We both chose the mild soup. However, the first bite was still a little spicy for me. The word "mild" did not mean the soup would taste the same to both of us. I drank some water and ate more slowly.

"Next time, I'll choose less spicy soup," I said. "And fewer noodles?" Mina asked with a smile. I looked at my big bowl and laughed. Her joke reminded me of my choices. The food was good, but sharing this new experience with Mina was the best part.
variants.prestudy:
Last Saturday, I went to a malatang restaurant with my friend Mina. It was my first visit, so I did not know how to choose my food. Mina told me to pick the things I wanted to eat.

I put noodles, cabbage, mushrooms, and tofu into my bowl. Everything looked delicious, and I reached for more noodles. "Your bowl is already full!" Mina said with a laugh. I was choosing with my eyes instead of thinking about how much I could eat.

We both chose the mild soup. Although it was called "mild," the first bite was still a little spicy for me. The same word on a menu does not tell us exactly how everyone will feel. I drank some water and ate more slowly.

Next time, I will choose less spicy soup and think more carefully about the amount of food. "And fewer noodles?" Mina asked with a smile. I looked at my big bowl and laughed. She did not need to give me a long lesson. Her short question helped me notice something for myself. The food was good, but enjoying a new experience with a friend mattered most.
